labels.reason: The URL value from whistle rule configuration is concatenated into a link href attribute with no HTML/attribute escaping, so a crafted rule value can break out of the attribute in the injected page.
$ldap_loginsmb comes from the administrator-managed LDAP directory rather than from request input, so attackers do not realistically control it.
Only $_SERVER['PHP_SELF'] (which Dolibarr's main.inc.php checks for injection) and the numeric $object->id are concatenated into the href.
showdocuments receives a dol_sanitizeFileName-cleaned ref, a server-built directory and a URL made from PHP_SELF and the numeric id, so no unescaped user data reaches the output.
The form action is built only from PHP_SELF, which main.inc.php checks for script injection, and no other user data is placed on the line.
The link is built only from PHP_SELF and the integer user id, with no attacker-controlled HTML.
req.url, which the attacker controls, is put unescaped into an HTML 404 response (both the href and the link text) by the dev/preview server's not_found handler.

$group is concatenated unquoted into the SQL, and one caller (the SOAP webservice in server_user.php) passes request-supplied group_id after only a loose '> 0' check that strings like '1 OR 1=1' pass.
The content-type slugs come from Bolt's contenttype/field configuration, not from request data, and the order is whitelisted by fixOrder while the limit is cast to int.
get_resource_inst calls exists() before building resources, and exists() checks the table name against SHOW TABLES, so the DESCRIBE table name is limited to real table names.
hostId is a server-generated randomUUID and the island content is built internally by Astro (encrypted props and script-safe stringification), not from raw attacker HTML.

srcSchema/targetSchema are put unquoted into a shell command, but the shown context does not reveal whether they come from the uploaded backup or are checked by the assertPostgresSchemaIdentifier helper defined in this file.
The checkpoint name passed into workflow execution is put straight into a filename under the checkpoints directory with no sanitization or containment check, so '../' can write JSON outside it.
The SSID (even if broadcast by an attacker) goes through util.sanitizeString/sanitizeShellString, which strips shell metacharacters and quotes, before it is put into the quoted netsh argument.
The only external filter is 'statut = '.$search_statut in hierarchy.php, a numeric search parameter checked with >= 0; other callers pass no filter.

delete_session builds the path from the caller-supplied name (e.g. CLI /session delete args) with no sanitization or containment check before unlink, allowing traversal to delete arbitrary .json files.
The line prints Project::getNomUrl() built from DB-stored project ref and title, and whether that method escapes them is not shown (the resolved helper is a different class).
The script URL from whistle rule values is concatenated into a script src attribute with no attribute escaping, so a quote in the value injects markup or script into the proxied page.
output_path from workflow params is used directly for makedirs and save, and _validate_rotate_params only checks that it is present, so arbitrary write locations are possible.
contentType['slug'] comes from Bolt's ContentType configuration, the order is whitelisted by fixOrder and the amount is an int, so no request data reaches the SQL.
All shown callers pass integer group IDs taken from fetched objects (card.php group/card.php, LDAP sync script), with no raw request string reaching the unquoted SQL.
select_input/optionlist HTML-escape the $_GET order value with h(), and $i is an integer counter, so the reflected value is encoded.
$ldap_lastname is read from the administrator-managed LDAP directory, not from attacker-controlled request input.
$rid is escaped and comes from integer rights IDs (perms pages or module install), $module/$perms come from the rights_def table, and the callers need permission-editing rights.
$ldap_mail comes from the administrator-managed LDAP directory record, not from request input.
$column is produced by select_input, which HTML-escapes the $_GET column value through optionlist/h(), and $i is an integer.
options.historyLimit comes from the tool's caller-supplied options and is put into a shell command executed via exec with no runtime numeric validation (the TypeScript type is not enforced).
$ldap_mobile comes from the administrator-managed LDAP directory, not from attacker-controlled input.
$ldap_mail is LDAP directory data controlled by the directory administrator, not by an attacker.
Only PHP_SELF and the integer user id are concatenated into the href.
getGitHash is only called with the constant 'HEAD' (from buildCacheKey), so no attacker-controlled ref reaches execSync.
$rid is escaped and integer-sourced, $module/$perms come from the rights_def table, and the callers (perms pages) need permission-editing rights and pass numeric IDs.

In safeMode the scheme check isSafeUrl runs on the raw destination before resolveBackslash/normalization, so a destination like 'javascript\:alert(1)' passes the check and is then rendered as an executable javascript: href.
The Revue importer is an admin-only import that already emits item.description as raw HTML by design, so the unescaped url adds no capability beyond the trusted importer's content.
Only PHP_SELF and the integer user id are concatenated into the href.
batchExecute is a generic query-builder sink whose SQL comes from the _insertBatch/_updateBatch/_upsertBatch render methods, and their key/value escaping is not shown.

The img attributes use the same pre-normalization scheme check, and the alt text is built by regex tag-stripping of rendered inner HTML, which can leave a raw quote that breaks out of the alt attribute.
The sessionId query parameter is joined into a file path with no traversal check, so '../' sequences let any (CORS-enabled) caller read arbitrary .jsonl files outside the hooks data directory.
formconfirm receives only PHP_SELF plus the numeric object id and translated strings, so no attacker HTML is placed on the line.
